To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the monensin increased the proportion of propionate in the rumen, but did not alter ruminal fermentation or the concentrations of any of the blood metabolites measured.
monensin addition did not alter portal, hepatic or hepatic arterial flow but did increase the molar proportion of propionate and decreased isobutyrate and isovalerate in rumen fluid.
feeding monensin to cattle fed alfalfa hay increased ruminal propionate concentration, and increased arterial L-lactate and beta-hydroxyl butyrate concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of feeding monensin to steers on nutrient flux in the liver.
the effects of monensin on the metabolism of nutrients by the ruminant animal.
the influence of monesin on rumen fermentation and the effects of this change on net portal and liver metabolism of nutrients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

feeding of monensin at the level used in this experiment did not change portal or hepatic nutrient flux, but it did increase arterial L-lactate concentration and hepatic arterial beta-hydroxy butyrate concentrations in steers fed alfalfa hay plus corn.
monensin addition had no effect on the net portal or hepatic flux of any of the nutrients measured.
feeding monensin did not alter the portal and hepatic flux of any of the metabolites measured in steers fed a diet of chopped alfalfa hay with finely ground corn added.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monensin did not alter net hepatic nutrient flux when added to a low-quality forage diet.
the addition of monensins to a high quality alfalfa hay ration had no effect on nutrient metabolism.
monensin did not affect nutrient flux in the steers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of monensins to an alfalfa diet does not change the flux of nutrients through the liver.
monensin does not affect nutrient flux from the gut to the liver.
monensin addition did not affect the hepatic or portal nutrient flux of the major nutrients (glucose, lactate, and amino acids).
